_comment: Scripted model replies for LLM_PROVIDER=fake (tutor_api/llm/fake.py): the browser end-to-end flows and the local compose stack. Every prompt gets the same three-block circuit (a 300 Hz sine, an RC low-pass whose first draft has a wrong pin, a follower); a word in the prompt picks a variant: e2e-cancel and e2e-reload hold the filter's composer, e2e-retry fails the planner once, e2e-unsupported asks for what no template builds. Ask: e2e-ask answers about the RC filter with an experiment (R1 to 16k), e2e-ask-fail is a model outage, e2e-ask-slow holds its answer 30 s; any other question gets a note that this is the scripted tutor. What changed: an edit to R1 is explained citing R1, C1, the filter block and its output; any other change gets the same note.

uncovered: a microcontroller that reads the temperature

blocks.title: Test signal
blocks.purpose: V1 makes a 300 Hz sine wave to test the filter with.

blocks.title: Low-pass filter
blocks.purpose: R1 and C1 let low frequencies through and send high ones to ground.

blocks.title: Output buffer
blocks.purpose: U1 copies the filtered signal so a load cannot change the corner frequency.

rules.reply: This circuit filters a test signal. A sine source drives an RC low-pass filter, which passes slow signals and shunts fast ones to ground. An op-amp follower then buffers the result.

requirements.evidence: The source block supplies the filter input at 300 Hz.
The assembled filter passed its cutoff check.
The follower is connected after the filter.
This scripted demo always builds the same circuit; use a configured model to review a custom request.

rules.reply:
[R1] and [C1] set the corner of [block:b2]: \(f_c = \frac{1}{2\pi RC}\). A larger [R1] charges [C1] more slowly, so the corner of the RC filter [block:b2] moves down. [R9] is not in this circuit.
